framing: The quarterly architecture decision process is structured to surface contradictions in evidence rather than average them away; each decision lever is evaluated against a defined theme with explicit confidence thresholds derived from evidence spread, volume, and transfer distance.
components: Each component includes a claim, supporting keys, strongest counter-evidence, and one sentence on what the pack cannot resolve. Components are named explicitly: classical baseline, dense-retrieval result, zero-shot benchmark, hybrid routing study, engineering cost study, reranking economics note. Each carries field names, value types, closed vocabularies, and exact strings as identifiers. All components are self-contained and actionable without reference to others.
specificity_notes: Confidence values are justified by evidence spread, volume, or transfer distance; no intuition is used. Evidence recency is marked explicitly for all facts. Units are included in every numeric label. All scales, ratings, and bands are operationally defined before first use. Negative space is stated: this artifact does not include domain shifts beyond the six supplied items, nor does it incorporate external data sources or merge evidence from unverified studies.
acceptance_checks: Every claim must be reproducible from the source pack; all numbers match exactly as derived. Each judgment names its basis in the provided material. The process halts on input that cannot be classified with a diagnostic naming the offending input. Rounding and ordering rules are stated and followed consistently. A domain reviewer will spot-check three specific claims against raw data, and any deviation or ambiguity must be explicitly addressed.
